title: Overexpose
description: A summer sky through a pine, developed live on colour negative film. It opens on the normal print, deep cobalt behind dark pines; drag up to overexpose it by as much as three stops. The light is multiplied before the film sees it, and each layer of the negative climbs its own long soft shoulder, so where a phone sensor would clip the clouds to flat white the cobalt thins to a pale white-blue, the cumulus compress towards cream and keep their edges, and the shadows open. The diffusion and halation grow with the light over the shoulder.
intent: Genre spec idea 5, after Rinko Kawauchi's overexposed 6x6 colour (Utatane, Illuminance): show why film looks dreamy and digital looks cheap with one gesture, exposure, on real linear radiance through per-layer H&D curves and a print curve. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinko_Kawauchi
sources: HDRI: Tree Lined Driveway, Poly Haven, photographed by Dimitrios Savva, processed by Jarod Guest, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/tree_lined_driveway (8k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/8k/tree_lined_driveway_8k.hdr). Worm's-eye view lying under the pines: stereographic projection, 90 deg field, pitched +59 deg towards the zenith at yaw +222 deg from the panorama centre, rolled -2 deg, 1536 px square (every pass below up to the last two was made at an earlier aim, 116 deg at pitch +76, yaw +150, and carried over by reaim.py, first to 116 deg at pitch +66, yaw +178, then to this one). The sun is moved behind the top-centre pine. No camera aim can do that (in this HDRI it stands in open sky about 20 deg from the nearest crown, and turning the camera carries the crown along), so its disc, 16-ray diffraction star and aureole are painted out of the equirect, then the frame's open sky is fitted as an elevation gradient plus a radial term around the old sun, and only the radial term is moved to a new direction 2 deg inside that crown's lower edge, with the measured, ray-free circumsolar excess added there, on sky pixels only with a 1-2 px feather. Around the sun the crown is rebuilt as a hard silhouette at its own dark density, and needles on its open-sky edge in the sun's forward lobe get a thin (about 2 px) warm-white transmitted rim, scaled to outshine the sky beyond. The pale ghost the painted-out sun still left is removed in the camera frame: on open sky 10-48 deg from the new sun (thin cloud excluded by its whiteness against the fit), the sky is replaced by the fitted elevation gradient with no old-sun radial term, and the photograph's grain is re-added, matched in amplitude, grain size and channel correlation from open sky far from both suns. Then the open sky's smooth field is refitted and replaced by one that depends on zenith angle alone, darkest and most saturated overhead (printing about #2f6fc0 at 0 EV) and paler towards the low sky at the frame's edges, times a tight circumsolar glow around the hidden sun; only each pixel's sky share takes the change (read from blue-over-red chroma, and from luminance on the rim), so needles, the rim and cloud keep their light and the photograph's grain rides along as a ratio. The sky therefore deepens towards the zenith instead of paling towards an empty patch. The canopy's edges are then decontaminated: within 6 px of the open sky (and in the lit pockets of the crown around the hidden sun) each pixel's sky share is read from luminance between the local needle colour and the old sky behind it, the needle colour is solved as (C - t S_old) / (1 - t) and the pixel re-composited over the new sky, so the old pale sky no longer outlines the crowns in cream. Shipped as log2 radiance -8.5..+2.5 in 8 bits with TPDF dither (scene.webp), with the diffusion and halation blurs baked from the same radiance (optics.png). Last, the cumulus are relit: each pixel's cloud share is keyed from the scene (neutral and bright), blurred to the scale of puffs and banks, and the side of each blob that faces the frame's edge (away from the zenith, read from the blurred key's gradient) is multiplied towards skylight blue (#b8cde6), as is the part of a bank that more cloud shades from the hidden sun, while the sun-facing tops get a slight warm lift; the key ships as scene.webp's alpha, so the piece can hold everything but the cloud back as it overexposes and the clouds climb the print's shoulder above the sky. Last, the hidden sun is lit again, about 2-3 stops above what the earlier steps left of it: a near-white cyan aureole on the sky share around it (12x the local sky at the sun, falling off over 1.6 and 7 deg), a few sharp, un-blurred sparkles of the disc in the crown's real pin-hole gaps within 4 deg (one hot pixel and a faint short glint each), the crown's own needle mass deepened about 0.6 stop around the sun so it prints as the darkest silhouette in the frame, and, on the crown's open-sky edge in the sun's forward lobe, a transmitted fringe feathered over about 4 px into the needles: its light is the sky and aureole behind it (so cyan-white, not a colour of its own), scaled by the needles' local sky share and never more than 85% of that light, and mixed edge pixels take the aureole in their sky share, so the crown's lower lip ramps into the bloom instead of being outlined (an earlier 1.5 px warm-white rim printed as a crisp tan outline). The diffusion and halation are rebaked from that brighter light, and the disc's own light, which the encoding cannot hold, is added to the diffusion as a tight cyan-white veil around the hidden sun (falling off over 2.2 deg), weighted by the sky share (widened by the fringe, so it crosses the crown's lip) so it lands on the open sky around the crown and the needle mass keeps only 15% of it. The glow is keyed into the alpha as well (falling off over 9 deg, on the sky share; the needles take a fifth of it), so the printer's hold spares it: at 0 EV the crown is a dark silhouette with a glowing edge in a cyan-white bloom, and as the exposure rises the glow climbs the shoulder and swallows the crown's edge. Last of all, the open sky is graded as through a polariser (polarise.py), on sunburst.py's bake: its light (read on open blue sky only, with the old circumsolar excess divided out so the bright sky by the crown still counts, and thin cloud and puffs keeping their own excess) is replaced everywhere, with nothing of the old field kept near the sun, by a field that is strictly a function of the angle from the true zenith the pine trunks converge on: deep cobalt overhead (printing about rgb(32,104,184) at 0 EV, hue 212) opening out to about rgb(106,167,228) at the frame's mid-edges, both ends solved through the piece's negative and print so the hue stays at 210-212. It opens as a dome, not a cone: (z / 60 deg) ^ 2.8 in log radiance, eased into a soft cap past the rim, so the deep blue holds broad and level overhead and the print is only half-way to the rim some 45 deg out; the whole square reads as one cobalt dome deepening overhead (an earlier near-linear falloff from a darker rgb(24,90,170) printed as a tight dark disc, a bullseye at the frame's centre). On it the hidden sun's aureole is laid again, wider than sunburst.py's (17x the sky at the sun, falling off over 3 deg instead of 1.6, with a faint 6 deg edge in the sky's own blue, whitening only where it is strong), so it fades out instead of stopping at a hard rim and leaves no grey skirt. Only each pixel's sky share takes it: needles are kept out by a luminance share, and cloud by a continuous cloud-optical-depth matte, read as one minus the pixel's blue-minus-red saturation, (B - R) / B, over the local sky's and smoothed by a guided filter on the log luminance (wider in thin veils, tight at a cumulus's crisp edge), so the polariser's gain falls as (1 - depth) squared and thin wisps keep their pale, unpolarised brightness (a per-pixel chroma share had broken every thin edge into mottled deep-blue holes); the veils' leftover lace of half-sky speckle is pulled most of the way to that matte. In the same pass the cumulus are graded by depth and by the hidden sun's direction: the sun-facing tops, and what of the cloud the sun reaches without crossing more cloud, lift towards warm-neutral #f4f1ea, and the thick cores that cloud shades from the sun sink towards skylight blue #afc6de, only the cloud's own light in each pixel's cloud share, so half-sky edge pixels take no tan outline. Near the sun that share is also feathered about 5 px into the crown and that feathered part takes the aureole's light only, so the bloom bleeds into the lip's needles instead of being cut out around them. The grain rides along as a ratio, and the optics take the change's own blur. Then the canopy is made the frame's sharp anchor (canopy.py): each pixel is read as the open light behind it (a masked blur of confident sky and cloud) and the needle in front, its open share solved from blue-minus-red against the sky behind (from luminance where cloud is behind), and that matte is sharpened (an unsharp mask clipped to 0..1, then its middle pushed to the ends, so no halo is left on either side of the edge) while the needle colour's own texture is sharpened in log light; the needle share then goes down 1.3 stops, half-way towards the hue of #141a18, and the print paper's dense end is extended past the sky's densities so the darkest tenth prints about rgb(19,25,24) at 0 EV, with the Pro-Mist veil and halation capped on the needles at low exposure and the needles read from the full-size scene rather than its blurrier mip, so the softness stays in the sky and cloud. The top crown's smeared lower lip (the rebuild's soft, rounded lobes and a hanging lobe) is opened, trimmed to a slightly eroded edge laid with tufts of drawn needles leaning towards the zenith, and refilled with the polarised sky and aureole (levelled to the open sky around and carrying grain copied from open sky). (A drawn leader hanging from that lip on the line to the zenith read as a fern pasted on and was taken out again; the notch it hung from keeps sky and needle tufts on its walls.) The 8k caches being gone, the dome field and the leader's removal were put into the shipped bake by redome.py: open sky there is exactly grain times the old field, so each pixel's sky light (itself, up to 1.3x the old field) is multiplied by the new field over the old in its sky share, (1 - cloud depth) squared, and the leader is found as the thin dark structure the crown's lobes do not hold and repainted with the new sky, its alpha and grain. Last, the top crown is re-keyed from real needles (crown.py): the rebuilt, trimmed and deepened crown printed as a smooth, lumpy blob with drawn spiky tufts and the aureole showed only as a crescent under its lip, so the crown is recomposited from an earlier bake of the same frame that still holds the HDRI's own needles (same geometry, pixel for pixel): its open share solved against the old sky behind it and sharpened, its needle colour taken down as the other pines are (1.3 stops, half-way to #141a18, texture sharpened), and its sky share filled with the new sky and aureole. The aureole is re-laid on the whole sky share as a softened power law (17x the sky at the sun, 17 / (1 + (g / 2.6 deg) ^ 1.6), tapered past ~14 deg) rather than an exponential, so it eases out instead of stopping at a rim; near the sun the crown's thin foliage keeps (and amplifies) the little sky it holds, read as a faint haze plus pin-holes where it stands above its surroundings, the thinnest needles are eaten by irradiation (gaps grow by up to 3 px at the sun), and the disc sparkles in those pin-holes, so the hidden sun shows as a radial glow through the crown's own gaps. The sky hold's glow key and the disc's diffusion veil are laid again on the new sky share (the needle mass taking 45% of the veil instead of 15%, so the veil is a disc round the sun, not a crescent). Last, the cumulus are re-shaded from the HDRI's own unclipped radiance (clouds.py): the earlier grades read the clouds from the tone-mapped bake, whose chroma by then carried grain, old compression blocks and every later pass, so the banks printed as flat grey-white with cyan blotches where the cobalt leaked in. The 8k equirect, rendered through the same camera, lands on the bake pixel for pixel (the cloud pixels were never moved). Each pixel's cloud depth is read from it (one minus its blue-minus-red saturation over the local open sky's, gated by luminance against the needles and filled under them, and only where the bake's old cloud key was, so the old sun's star and the crown's glow are left alone); the cloud's own light is solved out of the mixed edge pixels, and its log over the banks' top light, eased as 3.6 (1 - exp(-x / 1.0)) stops, sets the shade, with a +/-0.35 stop lift on the side of each puff that faces the hidden sun. The colour follows the shade: warm-neutral on the lit tops, skylight blue (hue about 207, 27-36% saturation at mid value) in the shaded bases. Each open pixel is recomposited as (1 - depth) x the bake's local open sky plus depth x that cloud light, so inside a bank no sky chroma gets through; needle pixels change only in their open share, never losing more than a quarter of any channel. The sky hold's key (alpha) is laid again from the new depth, sunburst.py's glow key kept under it, and the optics take the change's own blur. In the piece, a cloud highlight (on that key, off the sky) takes cloudWarm more red than blue before the paper-white cap, so the tops roll off towards #fff6ea on the shoulder and never reach 255. Last, the pines are rebuilt from the HDRI's own radiance (foliage.py), as the cumulus are: the 8k equirect rendered through the same camera (3x supersampled) lands on the bake pixel for pixel, and each pixel is unmixed in linear RGB between the light behind it (a normalised-convolution blur of the open sky and cloud round it) and the local needle colour, alpha = (B - C).(B - F) / |B - F|^2, so the matte is the photograph's own sub-pixel coverage: a twig a third of a pixel wide keeps a third of its pixel, and the needle sprays, the bare branches of the diagonal pine and the crowns' fringes are as fine as the lens left them, with no threshold. Only pixels near real needles count (cloud shading is not foliage), a small dead zone (0.04-0.12) takes out the sky's noise, and coverage over 0.9 is solid. The ink is the needle mass's own radiance, the pixel itself where it is solid and solved out of the mix, (C - (1 - a) B) / a, where it is thin, taken down by one gain (about 1.4 stops) so the median needle prints near-black at 0 EV as before, and 40% of the way to #141a18's hue, but keeping all of its own relief (about 2.2 stops between the 5th and 95th percentile), so as the exposure lifts the shadows the lit needles, branches and hollows open up as photographed. The plate under the trees, and a strip at the right edge the earlier repaints had smeared, is rebuilt from the same render with the needles taken out, shaded into cloud light as clouds.py shades it, over the clean dome field of the open sky (polarise.py's dome and crown.py's aureole, with a low-order correction fitted to the bake's open sky) times grain matched to the photograph's (amplitude, grain size and channel correlation measured on open sky), with the cloud key laid again from the new depth; the optics take the change. The crown within 9-13 deg of the hidden sun is left to crown.py. The ink and its matte ship as trees.webp, laid over the sky after the Pro-Mist and the halation; the printer's sky hold is applied to the sky seen through a spray and to the needles over it each by its own light before they mix, so no part-covered pixel escapes the hold as a pale ring. The ink takes none of the veil and a tenth of the halation at 0 EV, rising to the full amounts by +2 EV as the shadows open. Last, the cumulus are given back their photographed structure (cumulus.py): next to the rebuilt pines the banks printed as airbrushed cotton, because clouds.py had shaded them through a 2x render with a cloud light eased and, outside the solid cores, blurred over 6 px. The plate is re-solved from the same 3x supersampled render as the pines, with the needles unmixed out first: the cloud depth matte is the HDR's own, per pixel at 1536 px (blue-minus-red saturation lost against the local sky), not blurred, its edge tightened by an unsharp mask clipped to each pixel's 3x3 range so a turret's rim is crisp and a thin veil stays soft, and wherever a bank is thick (its 5 px local depth over 0.7-0.9) it is solid, so no sky chroma gets in (the cyan hole in the lower-centre bank is gone). The cloud's light keeps the photograph's luminance above lobe scale (16 px, at 1.2x, the shadows between lobes at 1.8x from 7 px inside the edge, the finest band lifted a further 0.8x), and clouds.py's depth-and-light shade, sun-facing lift and warm-top / skylight-blue colour are kept only below that scale, as a slow multiplier. The open sky in an edge pixel is the clean dome field times matched grain, the cloud key (alpha) is laid again from the new depth at full resolution, and the optics take the change. In the piece the cloud is read from the full-size scene, as the needles are, so the Pro-Mist veil is the only softening it gets: at 0 EV the banks print sharp-edged, and they bloom as the exposure climbs. Last, the camera is re-aimed at the cumulus (reaim.py): at pitch +76 the upper-left and centre of the square were empty cobalt and the banks small puffs at the right and bottom edges, so it is turned 28 deg towards the lower-right bank and lowered to +66 deg. The open blue becomes a band overhead under the hidden sun's crown, the diagonal pine stands up with its trunk converging on the zenith, and the banks fill the lower half of the square. Every pass is a function of the direction on the sky (the dome of zenith angle alone, the aureole of the angle from the hidden sun, which keeps its direction), so the bake is carried over exactly: each new pixel's ray, where it fell inside the old frame, takes the old scene, key, ink and matte from there (Lanczos on the log codes; the scale changes by under 16%). The low sky the new aim reveals (about a fifth of the square) starts as the clean dome field times matched grain, and the pines and cumulus are then solved again everywhere from the 8k HDR through the new camera, exactly as foliage.py and cumulus.py solved them, so the carried-over and the new parts meet with no seam. The far hillside the lowest corner now shows under the horizon (under 2% of the square) is laid in the ink layer at full coverage at the needles' own gain, so it prints dark at 0 EV and opens to its sunlit green as the exposure climbs; the optics are rebaked from the new visible scene, with the old disc veil carried over. Then the camera is re-aimed again (reaim.py, second run): the 116 deg square still had no subject, an empty band of cobalt across the upper middle, small puffs along the edges and the far hillside in the lower-right corner, so the field is tightened to 90 deg (the clouds print about 1.34x larger at the centre) and turned 44 deg towards the bank at the old frame's lower right, lowered to +59 deg and rolled to -2 deg. That bank now fills the lower middle between the diagonal pine on the left and the round pine on the right, the deep cobalt holds the upper middle, and the hidden sun's crown sits in the top-right corner with the sun at the top edge; no ray dips under 5.9 deg elevation and the pines hold both lower corners, so no horizon or hillside shows and the hillside layer is dropped. Nothing of the old bake is kept in the picture (it lends only its open sky to the dome's low-order fit, its grain statistics and its ink's median): the open sky is laid fresh everywhere as the clean dome field, polarise.py's dome times crown.py's aureole as a function of the angle from the hidden sun, times grain matched to the photograph's at the bake's own scale (the tighter field would otherwise magnify the old plate and its grain by up to 1.4x), and all three pines and the cumulus are solved again from the 8k HDR through the new camera by foliage.py's and cumulus.py's solves. That includes the crown that hides the sun: an earlier run carried crown.py's crown over within 20-27 deg of the sun, and it printed as the smeariest silhouette in the frame (a soft, rubbery lip, a hanging wisp doubled by the resampling, blurred blobs for needle sprays), its feather meeting the fresh dome along a straight diagonal seam. Now it is unmixed from the HDR's radiance as the other pines are, so its sprays are as fine as the lens left them, and the hidden sun is laid again on the fresh sky share: the aureole lies in the dome behind the needles and shows through every real gap, within about 15 deg of the sun the thinnest needles are eaten by irradiation (the matte's gaps open by up to 2 px at the sun, falling off over 2.5 deg), the disc sparkles in the crown's real pin-holes within 6 deg (one hot pixel and a faint short glint each), and the sky hold's glow key is laid on the sky share with the needle mass taking a fifth of it, so the crown prints as dark as the other pines inside a cyan-white bloom. The optics are rebaked from the new visible scene, with the disc's own light added to the diffusion as a tight veil weighted by the new sky share (the needle mass keeping 45% of it). Bake: tools/depth/bakes/overexpose (desun.py, resun.py, deepen.py, bake_wormseye.py, relight.py, sunburst.py, polarise.py, canopy.py, redome.py, crown.py, clouds.py, rekey.py, foliage.py, cumulus.py, reaim.py run twice).
